turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Morning. Pressure outside is one fifty two over eighty eight, pulse seventy eight. He kept saying it is nothing only.
[SEG0002] person_2 (DOCTOR): Mm. Come, sit. What is the problem.
[SEG0003] person_3 (PATIENT): No problem as such doctor. I am sixty eight, old age only. My wife dragged me.
[SEG0004] person_2 (DOCTOR): Urine?
[SEG0005] person_3 (PATIENT): Uh, getting up in the night. Three times, four times. Everyone does that, no?
[SEG0006] person_2 (DOCTOR): Not everyone. Stream is weak?
[SEG0007] person_3 (PATIENT): Little bit weak, yes. Well, actually mornings are worse. I am managing, it is not a big thing.
[SEG0008] person_2 (DOCTOR): Dribbling after you finish?
[SEG0009] person_3 (PATIENT): Few drops in the underwear, sometimes. I don't even look.
[SEG0010] person_2 (DOCTOR): How long.
[SEG0011] person_3 (PATIENT): Err, the tea. My wife boils it very strong, two cups after dinner, she will not reduce. And the traffic today was mad, we left the house at seven.
[SEG0012] person_2 (DOCTOR): Tea later. How long are you getting up at night.
[SEG0013] person_3 (PATIENT): Some months only. Three months, four months, I don't count. Around Diwali maybe. I can't say the date.
[SEG0014] person_2 (DOCTOR): Blood in the urine?
[SEG0015] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Never.
[SEG0016] person_2 (DOCTOR): Burning?
[SEG0017] person_3 (PATIENT): Not that either.
[SEG0018] person_2 (DOCTOR): Pain?
[SEG0019] person_3 (PATIENT): No, it is not painful.
[SEG0020] person_2 (DOCTOR): Fever? Weight down?
[SEG0021] person_3 (PATIENT): No fever. Weight is the same. I am eating.
[SEG0022] person_2 (DOCTOR): You are on treatment for pressure. Which tablet.
[SEG0023] person_3 (PATIENT): Amlodipine, five mg, morning, since many years. One tablet.
[SEG0024] person_2 (DOCTOR): Every day?
[SEG0025] person_3 (PATIENT): Mostly. Sometimes I skip, if I am feeling alright. The reading is fine, what is there.
[SEG0026] person_2 (DOCTOR): One fifty two is high. Don't skip it. Giddiness when you stand?
[SEG0027] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Well, sometimes, if I get up fast from the bed. It goes.
[SEG0028] person_2 (DOCTOR): Chest pain? Short of breath?
[SEG0029] person_3 (PATIENT): Not that either. Nothing of that.
[SEG0030] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any surgery before.
[SEG0031] person_3 (PATIENT): No. Never went for an operation.
[SEG0032] person_2 (DOCTOR): Drug allergy?
[SEG0033] person_3 (PATIENT): Umm. No. Nothing like that.
[SEG0034] person_2 (DOCTOR): Smoking? Drink?
[SEG0035] person_3 (PATIENT): Never smoked. One small peg on a Sunday, sometimes only. I am retired now, accounts in the mill, that life is over.
[SEG0036] person_2 (DOCTOR): Father or brother, prostate problem?
[SEG0037] person_3 (PATIENT): Father had the same, up in the night. He went to eighty four. So I am not fussed.
[SEG0038] person_2 (DOCTOR): Any tablet earlier for this, finasteride or dutasteride?
[SEG0039] person_3 (PATIENT): Finesteride, last year. Two months I took, then I stopped it in March. No use. Dutasteride I never took, nobody gave it.
[SEG0040] person_2 (DOCTOR): What dose was the finesteride.
[SEG0041] person_3 (PATIENT): Five mg I think, maybe. I threw the strip. Anyway I am not on it.
[SEG0042] person_2 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft. No tenderness over the bladder. No rectal exam today.
[SEG0043] person_3 (PATIENT): Good. All this fuss for a small thing.
[SEG0044] person_2 (DOCTOR): This is most likely the prostate, the night frequency, weak stream and dribbling. Not final until the tests.

[SEG0045] person_2 (DOCTOR): Urine test today, give it before you leave. Thursday morning, blood for PSA, sister will take it. No fasting. No heavy exercise, no cycling, no relations for two days before that blood.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): Urine pot is ready. Thursday eight thirty I have kept for the PSA. He need not fast.
[SEG0047] person_2 (DOCTOR): If the PSA is borderline we do a free PSA. If this does not settle, then a scan of the bladder and prostate. Not booked now.
[SEG0048] person_2 (DOCTOR): Starting tamsulosin zero point four mg, one capsule at night. It can increase the giddiness, so get up slowly. And no tea after six.
[SEG0049] person_3 (PATIENT): Another tablet. If you insist. Tea, she will shout, but I will try. It is nothing serious.
[SEG0050] person_2 (DOCTOR): I will see you in two weeks with the reports. If you cannot pass urine at all, come sooner, do not sit at home.
[SEG0051] person_1 (NURSE): Sample before you go sir. Thursday eight thirty. And no heavy exercise, like doctor said.

spec.situation: Older man getting up three to four times at night, weak stream, dribbling; drinks tea in the evening; denies blood in urine; PSA and urine tests planned, tamsulosin discussed.

traps.happens: In the plan the doctor books some tests or visits for a definite time ('the nurse takes bloods Thursday morning', 'I'll see you in two weeks') and makes others conditional ('if those are borderline we do the third test', 'if it does not settle, a scan').
traps.label_rule: Booked or arranged = status planned. Only the hedged ones are conditional. Never mark a booked test conditional or 'if needed'. Instructions for the booked test (fasting, time, medicine timing) belong to that test's action, not a separate invented plan item.

traps.happens: The patient denies some symptoms (said as 'no', 'not really', 'never'), has a chronic condition named earlier (for example asthma or hypertension) and later the doctor asks about another symptom of it, and one answer is a double negative or a correction ('not that either', 'no... well, sometimes').
traps.label_rule: Denials go in negative_findings with the exact thing denied, never in symptoms. NEVER write a negative about a condition the patient has said they have. A corrected answer keeps only the final version. A negative is never a symptom, and 'not painful' is the finding 'pain' absent, not a symptom called 'painless'.

features: patient_answers_other_question: the patient answers a different question than the one asked, and the doctor repeats or lets it go.

stopped_or_never_taken: a medicine the patient stopped, was never given or only took once ('I stopped it in March'). Status discontinued, not current; a medicine never taken is not recorded as a medication.

bad.reason: Stopped finasteride after 2 months is supported; dose 5 mg is uncertain, and indication not explicitly stated.
